PMN intracellular killing activity is reduced in RRMS patients, regardless of their disease stage or therapeutic management.
PMN functional impairment is present in RRMS patients and that this impairment is independent from the stage of the disease and from the type of therapy.

PMNs from relapsing remmiting MS patients have a statistically significant reduction in intracellular microbial killing activity, which is not related to the disease stage or to the therapeutic management.

the study of the functional activity of PMNs in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis patients.
the study of PMN functional activity in patients with relapsing remiting multiple sclerosis.
the role of PMNs in the immune response in patients with MS, with the aim of identifying a subset of these patients who are more susceptible to microbial infections.

the PMN functional activity of MS patients is impaired.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the impairment of PMNs function in multiple sclerosis patients is not related to the disease activity, but rather to the treatment, and that this impairment is not associated with the production of proinflammatory cytokines, reactive oxygen species or apoptosis.
the innate immunity of MS patients is not altered in a way that would make them prone to infection, although the functional activity of their PMNs is significantly reduced.
PMNs from multiple sclerosis patients are functionally impaired, independently from their disease stage and treatment.

the functional impairment of polymorphonucloear leukocytes in relapsing multiple sclerosis patients is not related to the disease stage, and is not dependent on the type of immunotherapy.
